children: The order, secured through its US subsidiary Global Impx, comes less than three months after the unit joined the Blue Cloud group and covers end-to-end AI infrastructure services in New Jersey

Shares of Blue Cloud Softech Solutions rose about 2 per cent on the BSE in early trade on Friday after the company said its US subsidiary, Global Impx Inc., had secured a Rs 147 crore (USD 15.5 million) order from IBM Cloud Inc. for an AI infrastructure project in New Jersey.
The contract covers the design, deployment and support of a GPU-powered artificial intelligence infrastructure platform for enterprise AI workloads.
The fixed-fee contract, worth about Rs 147 crore, comes less than three months after Global Impx joined the Blue Cloud group, the company said in an exchange filing.

Work on the project began on September 24 and will be delivered in five milestones, from project kick-off through production go-live, Blue Cloud said. The companies signed a master services agreement on August 21.

Global Impx will build an infrastructure environment for AI and machine-learning workloads, including model development, training, fine-tuning and inference. Its scope covers architecture and design, deployment of GPU compute clusters, high-performance storage and networking, AI/ML platforms and Kubernetes-based orchestration.

The engagement also includes security and operational services such as identity and access controls, network segmentation, encryption, monitoring, backup and disaster recovery, followed by performance validation, documentation, knowledge transfer and production handover.

The project carries service-level commitments including at least 99.5 per cent availability for infrastructure and GPUs, notification of critical alerts within 15 minutes and response to critical incidents within 30 minutes.
"AI is moving out of the lab and into production, and that move runs on infrastructure," Blue Cloud Group Chairman Tejesh Kumar Kodali said.
The order marks an early commercial win for Global Impx following its acquisition by Blue Cloud, with the company seeking to expand its US-based AI infrastructure business.
Blue Cloud Group CEO Vinod Babu Bollikonda said its teams had already been mobilised and that the company would execute the project against agreed milestones and service levels.
The order comes as companies and cloud providers expand spending on computing infrastructure to support the growing demand for AI model training and inference.
